finding.claim: The error returned by Authorize is discarded, so the 'dba' role check is never enforced on /admin/drop. Any caller that reaches the handler can run DROP TABLE. The table name is also concatenated into the SQL, which allows SQL injection.
finding.source: HTTP request to /admin/drop by any user, including a non-dba user. The form value 't' is attacker-controlled.

trace.note: u := userFrom(r) gets the user from the request context
Authorize(u, "dba") returns an error that is ignored, so execution continues for non-dba users
The unvalidated form value t is concatenated into the DROP TABLE statement and passed to runSQL

finding.guards_checked: Authorize is called but its result is unused. Compare vacuum at api.go:33, which checks err and returns 403. There is no identifier allowlist or quoting on t. No auth middleware is registered in main, since the handler is mounted directly with http.HandleFunc. userFrom also panics via an unchecked type assertion if no user is in the context, which is a DoS at worst and not an authorization bypass.

verdict.guard_found: Authorize (api.go:13-20) returns an error, but dropTable discards it at api.go:26. Separately, userFrom (api.go:22) does an unchecked type assertion on a context value that nothing in the repo sets. No WithValue call exists, and main at api.go:44 registers no middleware. The request therefore panics at api.go:25 before line 27, so it fails closed. There is no identifier allowlist or parameterization on t.
verdict.reason: The trace lines are accurate, and the discarded error at api.go:26 plus the concatenation at api.go:27 are real defects. But nothing in the repo ever puts a "user" into the request context (grep for WithValue and "user" finds only api.go:22). Every request to /admin/drop therefore panics at api.go:25, via the nil-interface assertion in userFrom at api.go:22, before runSQL runs. As shipped, the DROP and the injection are unreachable. The flaw is latent and becomes exploitable once any auth middleware populates the context, so it should still be fixed.
